extracted.intended_audience: Commissioner of Indian Affairs; Department of the Interior; Indian agents and agency administrators
extracted.subtask_description: An 1880 United States Indian agent annual report describing metrics and judgments for running an Indian agency: health/sanitation, education, agriculture, policing, housing, inter-tribal relations, and use of government resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitary condition / public health
rubrics_metrics.description: The sanitary condition of the tribe — improvement indicated by better nourishment, fewer deaths, less pulmonary disease, and reduced influence of superstitious native medical practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess sources of malaria (river overflows, slimy deposits on banks of Arkansas and Cimarron, small streams with stagnant mud), housing ventilation (avoid crowded unventilated mud lodges whose porous walls retain exhalations), clothing and comfortable dwellings, and availability/quality of a physician. Recommend bath-houses as sanitary measures. Examples: cracked sun-baked river deposits that can evolve malaria; physician competence steadily decreasing reliance on native doctors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freighting by Indians (logistics and economic effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Freighting operations performed by Indians evaluated by cost, losses/damage, efficiency, wages earned, and broader educational/civilizing effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare pay rates and costs (example: 50 cents per 100 pounds from Arkansas City with rations and occasional extra supplies; white freighters could be obtained at 40 cents; transporting from railroad terminus 15 cents per 100 cheaper). Look at loss/damage rates (reported as little loss), daily wages (meager), whether earnings are spent on family needs and purchasing wagons, and non-monetary benefits (manly and industrious habits, training). Operational notes: small teams, light loads, direction by farmer/assistant, need for prudent vigilant care to avoid mishaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerical work / administrative timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeliness and completeness of clerical and accounting work for annuities, wages, salaries, and expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate arrears, office workload, staffing adequacy (e.g., resignation of a key clerk caused backlog), and capacity to bring work up to departmental standards. Consider seasonality (arrival of annuity money near fiscal year-end) as a cause of press of work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education and schools (attendance, facilities, outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality and reach of education: day and boarding schools, attendance rates, boarding accommodations, and measurable student progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure average attendance (examples: day school average 20; multiple boarding/day-school enrollments listed), success indicators (monthly reports, letters from students, comparison to white schools), infrastructure needs (erect boarding-school buildings, room to accommodate target enrollments — e.g., target of 250 average attendance claimed), staffing/outsourcing (students sent to Carlisle Barracks), and special emphasis on educating girls/mothers as leverage for civilizing future generations. Note difficulties motivating children to attend when living far away.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing and agency buildings
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision, condition, and repair of private and agency housing and related furnishings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count and evaluate houses (e.g., number of log/box houses), carpentry outputs (bedsteads, cupboards, tables issued to families), issuance of cook-stoves and furniture, condition of agency buildings (commissary, school-house, employees' houses, shops), and need for maintenance (painting/repairs) and additional employee residences. Small investments in repairs are recommended as cost-saving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural productivity and crop management
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent and success of farming operations: acreage cultivated, crop yields, drought impact, pasture condition, haying, and encouragement of new crops (e.g., wheat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track acres planted and cultivated (examples: 100 acres corn and 5 acres potatoes planted; 2,528 acres cultivated on a reservation), effects of weather (protracted drought then copious rains), support measures (issuing seeds, breaking garden patches for needy families), hay-cutting capacity (mowing machines in use), pasture/grazing management, and plans to get more land broken and sow wheat. Recommend providing implements, stock, and incentives to break more land.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stock distribution and livestock management
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuance, condition, and stewardship of government-provided livestock (cows, heifers, bulls, work oxen, brood mares), and prevention of losses or premature disposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate numbers issued and retained (examples: 150 cows issued earlier with only ~100 remaining; 192 two-year-old heifers and 8 bulls issued to Poncas; 96 heifers and 4 bulls to Nez Perces), causes of losses (animals killed while tied to lariat, killed for feasts, straying), management practices, proposals to hold some animals as agency property until beneficiaries can manage them, and recommendations to prevent sale/disposal of gifted stock until recipients are self-sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Police organization and law enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Efficiency and organization of the agency police force; ability to prevent theft and enforce reservation rules (passes for non-residents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess police readiness and structure (reorganization planned where poor), responsiveness (readiness to perform duties), use of specific enforcement measures (ordering arrests of Osages found without a pass and escorting them off reservation), and risk management (incidents of attempted theft and potential for bloodshed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relations with neighboring tribes and diplomacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Character of inter-tribal relations, success of councils, and handling of grievances (redress, invitations to councils, and consequences of noncompliance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate cordiality except for known problem tribes (example: Osages), success or failure of negotiated councils (Osages agreed to council but failed to attend), impact on trust and willingness to entertain future propositions, and need for federal authority to secure justice and restore amicable relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal and resettlement policy / community stability
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of proposals or pressures to remove tribes back to former reservations and the impact of outside inducements on local stability and engagement in schooling/farming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure tribal preferences (Ponca leaders repeatedly stated they do not want to move), observe outside agents' efforts to hire Indians to leave, and note consequences for agricultural and educational progress. Consider land quality and sufficiency of current reservation (e.g., >100,000 acres, rich river bottoms) when making removal decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvements, renters, and saw-mill policy (infrastructure & economic development)
rubrics_metrics.description: Role of renters (white farmers) in making improvements, the renting-for-crop-share system, and the need for saw-mills to supply cheap lumber for building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh advantages and abuses of renting (renters often improve land for one-third of crop enabling Indians to gain improvements vs. potential dependency), observe that many improvements are made by white renters, and recommend authorization to use a saw-mill to produce lumber cheaply to increase housing construction and other improvements next year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitary infrastructure (bath-houses and related facilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of sanitary facilities such as bath-houses to improve public health at missions and schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend erecting bath-houses at mission schools and agencies (Seneca, Quapaw), arguing the investment will yield great returns in health improvements and is a high priority for sanitary measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral behavior, temperance, and vice prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: Promotion of temperance, religious observance, and measures to curb drinking, gambling, and other vices that hinder progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note successful temperance organizations and religious instruction (twice weekly services, Sabbath observance among Nez Perces), monitor rising vice (drunkenness, gambling) in some tribes, attempt moral suasion first but be prepared to adopt more efficient measures if ineffective. Encourage vocational training (blacksmith trade) as constructive alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of government resources and cost-effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate cost comparisons, effective use of funds, and the economic return of investments in schools, repairs, and supplies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare transport costs (Indian teamsters vs. white contractors; example: supplies hauled at cheaper rates with little loss), recommend small expenditures (painting/repairs, school accommodations) that yield outsized returns, and argue that educating wards is cheaper and more humane than war, with long-term social/economic benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent conduct and administrative philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended demeanor and policies for agents: treat Indians as men not children; be kind, firm, and just; inspire confidence; prioritize education and align all agency influences with agency objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents should avoid public criticism of predecessors, call attention to vital matters (educational forces, polygamy), propose departmental mandates to address harmful social practices (e.g., a mandate to stop polygamy and premature child marriage), and act to harmonize agency measures with the goals of civilization and education.
